sites.name: Kora

verifiedBusinessInfo.hours: Mon-Tue closed; Wed-Fri 7:30am-4pm; Sat-Sun 9am-4pm (Yelp listing, Nov 2026; single source, site tells visitors to check Instagram)
verifiedBusinessInfo.other: Co-founders Kimberly Camara and Kevin Borja; named for Camara's grandmother Corazon; began 2020 in a Woodside apartment after both were laid off from hospitality jobs; commissary kitchens and Alewife Brewery pick-ups; ~10,000-person waitlist; Sunnyside shop opened March 2025 (soft opening sold out in hours); won inaugural Queens' Best Bakery competition (Queens Chamber of Commerce), July 2025. Menu items: Leche Flan ni Lola (heirloom recipe of founder's late grandmother), Ube Fried Brioche, ube custard-filled doughnut, Salted Egg Ube Babka, Apple Fritter, croissants, scallion pancake croissant, ube ice cream sandwich (summer). No prices shown (only launch-era prices found).

sites.designDirection: A pastry-box identity for a Filipino-American doughnut bakery with a cult following: Bricolage Grotesque (condensed, heavy) paired with Instrument Serif italics, on an ube-violet / leche-flan caramel / cream / cocoa palette with a pandan-green accent. The hero is a giant KORA wordmark whose O is a slowly spinning doughnut-ring photo (radial mask), with an at-a-glance fact column and a rotating 'Queens' Best Bakery 2025' sticker; below, a sticky arched photo beside a dashed 'shelf' of four signature bakes, a sticky-headed story timeline on cocoa (2020 apartment kitchen to 2025 award), and a flan-orange visit card plus hours table. The menu page is a three-column bordered pastry-case board. Motion: ring spin, badge spin, soft scroll reveals; all disabled under reduced motion. Primary CTA: see the case / hours and directions.

sites.name: Route 66 Smokehouse

verifiedBusinessInfo.address: 79 Pearl Street, New York, NY 10004 (second entrance at 46 Stone Street; between Coenties Slip and Hanover Square)
verifiedBusinessInfo.hours: conflicting across sources (Stone Street district page: Mon-Wed 12pm-12am, Thu-Sat 12pm-2am, Sun 12pm-12am, kitchen closes 11pm; Yelp/others differ) - not shown; site says call ahead
verifiedBusinessInfo.other: Bourbon, brew and barbecue on Stone Street; Texas-style brisket and St. Louis ribs plus Southern riffs such as fried quail and waffles (Time Out); menu items per Yelp/blogs: sliced brisket, brisket sandwich, brisket sliders, beef ribs, pulled pork, smoked chicken; meats smoked in a basement pit (Glenwood); three spaces: year-round outdoor beer garden, indoor dining room, upstairs game room and lounge; bookable rooms listed on Tagvenue: 66 Lounge, Bar Cove, The Corner Cabana, Upstairs Game Room & Lounge, Outdoor Beer Garden; patio hosts 100+ guests.

sites.designDirection: A night-highway roadhouse for a FiDi after-work crowd: Big Shoulders Display (tall industrial condensed) with Barlow body and IBM Plex Mono mile-marker labels, on asphalt black, sodium-lamp orange, shield cream, centerline yellow, exit-sign green and brick red. The hero is a full-bleed overhead barbecue tray with a dark directional shade, mile-marker tags and a stacked poster headline, while an animated dashed yellow road centerline runs down the right edge. Sections read as a drive: a black felt letterboard 'pit list' beside a ribs photo, three green highway exit signs for the beer garden / dining room / upstairs game room, a sodium-orange events band, and a 'Destination' exit sign with big map/call rows. The events page lists the five bookable rooms with outlined numerals. Mobile adds a sticky Call / Directions bar. Primary CTA: call.

sites.name: Barchino

verifiedBusinessInfo.address: 502 Washington Boulevard, Jersey City, NJ 07310 (Apple Maps, Yelp); NOTE the official site reportedly lists 506 Washington Blvd
verifiedBusinessInfo.other: Pre-opening pizza-focused sister restaurant to Battello, next door on the Newport waterfront; chef/partner Ryan DePersio (also Battello, Ember & Eagle, The Kitchen Step); 120 seats; casual and approachable, moderate prices; planned pizzas (crispy, artisan-style, fresh seasonal toppings), paninis, shared plates, salads, appetizers, wine; events space; reservations and private events 'opening soon'; originally targeted fall 2026, latest report (Hoboken Girl, Nov 2026) early December 2026. Email info@barchinojc.com.

sites.designDirection: A Riviera boat-club announcement card for a pre-opening waterfront pizzeria (barchino is Italian for a little boat; its sister is Battello): Bodoni Moda high-contrast italics with Jost body, on marine navy, sail white, tomato red, sea glass, sand and basil. The hero hangs under a striped scalloped awning: a huge italic Barchino wordmark beside a bobbing porthole-framed margherita, over a notched boarding-pass strip (Port, Berth, Seats, Galley, Status). Below: planned menu categories as a column of CSS-drawn nautical signal flags with paired arch/rounded pizza photos, a navy 'crew' section with a facts manifest, a sand-colored opening log with a dotted route and a pulsing 'next' marker, and a sea-glass 'drop anchor' card with map buttons and contact rows. Single page because the restaurant has not published a menu yet. Primary CTA: follow on Instagram / directions.
